"It's true Ibra and Kaka have left Italy, but there are lots of great players in Italy and I am convinced I have made the best choice."

Eto’o displayed his new Inter shirt after finalizing his transfer from Barcelona on Monday. “For years I have wanted to play for Mourinho, but until now it has never happened,” he said.

“Ibrahimovic is an outstanding footballer, but I am Samuel Eto’o, and my achievements and history speak for themselves,” he said. “I do not like comparisons. I believe everything I have won so far gives my name its proper worth.”

During five seasons at Barcelona, Eto’o scored 125 times in 144 appearances. His goals helped the club collect numerous trophies, including three league championships, two Champions League titles and one Copa del Rey.

“Although I have always played in Spain, I have considerable experience in international competition,” Eto’o said. “Serie A has many top footballers, because great players choose clubs where they believe they can win trophies. I came here because this championship is highly competitive.

“It is true that Ibrahimovic and Kaka have departed Italy, but plenty of excellent players remain. I am certain that joining Inter was the best decision for me.”

## Inter unveil Samuel Eto’o

Inter Milan presented Samuel Eto’o as their new No. 9 in July 2009 after completing the high-profile deal that sent Zlatan Ibrahimović to Barcelona. The Cameroon striker said he had joined the Italian champions to keep winning rather than to be treated simply as Ibrahimović’s replacement.

Eto’o also stressed the importance of José Mourinho in his decision: “When Mourinho called me, I understood that he wanted me. I am very happy to be here and to be part of his project.”

Mourinho welcomed a forward who had already scored in two Champions League finals. “Eto’o is a great player and a great champion,” the Inter coach said. “He has won the Champions League twice and scored in both finals. Ibrahimović is a fantastic player, but Samuel has nothing to prove. He gives us different qualities and a winning mentality.”

### The Ibrahimović swap

The transaction was one of the biggest of the 2009 summer window:

- Ibrahimović moved from Inter to Barcelona.
- Eto’o went to Inter as part of the consideration.
- Barcelona paid Inter **€46 million in cash**.
- Eto’o was commonly valued at approximately **€20 million**, putting Ibrahimović’s nominal valuation at about **€66 million**.
- Alexander Hleb was initially expected to join Inter on loan as part of the arrangement, but he declined and moved to Stuttgart instead. Barcelona subsequently paid Inter an additional sum, widely reported as **€3 million**, in place of that element.
- Eto’o signed a **five-year contract** with Inter, reportedly worth about **€10–10.5 million net per season**.

### Eto’o’s record before joining Inter

Eto’o arrived with an elite scoring record:

- **Barcelona, 2004–09:** 130 goals in 199 competitive appearances.
- **La Liga for Barcelona:** 108 goals in 145 matches.
- **Mallorca:** 70 goals in 165 appearances in all competitions, including a then-club-record 54 league goals.
- **Barcelona honours:** three La Liga titles, two Champions League titles and one Copa del Rey.
- He scored in both the **2006 Champions League final against Arsenal** and the **2009 final against Manchester United**.
- In his final Barcelona season, 2008–09, he scored **36 goals in 52 appearances**, including 30 in La Liga.
- For Cameroon, contemporary records placed him at roughly **three dozen international goals in around 80 appearances**, with Olympic gold in 2000 and African Cup of Nations titles in 2000 and 2002.

The transfer effectively exchanged Inter’s leading star for a proven Champions League match-winner plus a substantial cash payment. Eto’o went on to become central to Mourinho’s side, which won the Serie A, Coppa Italia and Champions League treble in 2009–10.

## Barcelona–Inter Deal Swapped Eto’o for Ibrahimović

One of European football’s most memorable transfer deals took place in the summer of 2009, when Barcelona sent Samuel Eto’o to Inter Milan and brought Zlatan Ibrahimović to Camp Nou.

The agreement saw Barcelona pay Inter approximately **€45 million** in addition to handing over Eto’o. The move was intended to give Pep Guardiola’s European champions a different type of centre-forward, with Ibrahimović offering height, strength and technical creativity. Inter, meanwhile, acquired an established goalscorer entering the final year of his Barcelona contract.

Eto’o arrived in Italy after a hugely successful spell in Spain. He had scored in Barcelona’s 2006 and 2009 Champions League final victories and helped the club win a historic treble in his final season. Ibrahimović had been similarly influential at Inter, winning three consecutive Serie A titles and finishing as the league’s leading scorer in 2008–09.

Asked about comparisons between himself and Ibrahimović, Eto’o rejected the idea that the two should be directly measured against each other. He described Ibrahimović as a great player but stressed that they were different footballers with separate careers, adding that he preferred to let his own performances and trophies speak for him.

The deal ultimately worked far better for Inter. Under José Mourinho, Eto’o adapted to a tactically demanding role and helped the Italian club win the Serie A, Coppa Italia and Champions League treble in 2009–10. Inter eliminated Barcelona in the Champions League semifinals on the way to the title.

Ibrahimović scored regularly in Spain and won La Liga with Barcelona, but his relationship with Guardiola deteriorated. After only one season, he joined AC Milan on loan before completing a permanent move.

What initially appeared to be an expensive exchange of elite strikers therefore became a defining moment for both clubs: Eto’o immediately contributed to Inter’s greatest modern season, while Ibrahimović’s Barcelona career ended much sooner than expected.
